short: The longest continuous military campaign of the war, fought for control of the sea routes between North America and Europe.
full:
From the outbreak of war in September 1939, German U-boats and surface raiders sought to blockade the United Kingdom by sinking merchant shipping. The British, and later the Americans, relied on these Atlantic convoys for food, raw materials, and the military equipment necessary to continue fighting and eventually launch the liberation of Europe. The campaign saw continuous tactical and technological innovation from both sides.

The turning point came in May 1943, when Allied anti-submarine tactics, air cover, and codebreaking efforts inflicted unsustainable losses on the U-boat fleet. Securing the Atlantic supply lines allowed the Allies to build up the immense forces required for the invasion of Normandy. By the end of the war, over three thousand Allied ships had been sunk, but the German naval blockade had definitively failed.
